To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EP and LPS are immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive respectively in C3H mice.
endotoxin associated proteins are immunomodulators of C3H HeJ cells and lipopolysacharide endotoxins are immunosuppressors of C3HHeJ cells.
endotoxin associated proteins are potent stimulators of the immune response in C3H mice, whereas endotoxin is an inhibitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular events that occur during the interaction of endotoxin with cells of the immune system.
understanding the mechanisms of endotoxin action on C3H/ HeJ cells and the effects of LPS on EP induced C3H/HEJ cell responses.
the immunomodulation of endotoxin associated proteins (EP) and lipopolysaccarides (LPS) on C3H/ HeJ cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EP and LPS have opposing effects on C3H/ HeJ cell activation.
EP and LPS have different effects on the C3H/ HeJ B cell cycle and on the C3 H/HeJ macro phage and T cell proliferation.
EP is a potent B cell activator, LPS is a potent B and T cell inhibitor, and the two together can be used to study the mechanism of B cell activation and T cell inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EP and LPS are capable of stimulating a wide range of biological responses in the C3H/ HeJ cell.
LPS is able to inhibit EP induced B cell proliferation by down regulating PKC and that this inhibition extends to other cell types.
EP and LPS have opposite effects on C3H/ HeJ cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EP/LPS system is a useful model for studying endotoxin mediated immunomodulation.
EP and LPS can modulate C3H/ HeJ B lymphocyte activation and proliferation, but the mechanisms by which they accomplish this is different.
LPS can suppress the immune system in C3H HeJ mice.
